newsitem.title: INDIA: Doctors say Mother Teresa may never be as active.
newsitem.headline: Doctors say Mother Teresa may never be as active.

text.p: Doctors treating Mother Teresa said on Tuesday that the Nobel Peace Prize winner may take a very long time to recover from heart surgery and she may never be as active as before.
"It may be months or years from now," Dr Tarun Praharaj, a member of the team of doctors treating the renowned nun, told reporters in the eastern Indian city of Calcutta.
He had been asked when Mother Teresa would recover from last week's surgery to unblock to coronary arteries, her third such operation in five years.
Praharaj said the 86-year-old Roman Catholic missionary would go back to work at her Missionaries of Charity religious order once her heart and "other parameters" were declared satisfactory.
"But it will not be very, very active this time because we have to keep an eye on her health and monitor her parameters from time to time," he said. "It will not be as active as before."
Despite a series of health problems, Mother Teresa had kept up a seemingly tireless pace in her religious order before her latest illness and travelled widely.
Revered as a living saint for her work with the poor, the homeless and the terminally ill, Mother Teresa had surgery to clear two blocked arteries last week.
The nun, who was fitted with a heart pacemaker in 1989, had her first heart operation in the United States in 1991 and her second at the Birla centre in 1993.
She spent the weekend battling a long-standing lung problem and weak kidneys. She also had bronchial pneumonia.
Her doctors said on Tuesday they were optimistic the nun would quickly recover, but they cautioned that she remained in critical condition and was still not out of danger.

"Even though there are signs of slight improvement, we continue to be very concerned," the B.M. Birla Heart Research Centre said in a medical bulletin earlier on Tuesday. "She is still not out of danger, still critical."
Dr Patricia Aubanel of the United States said: "She is going to improve slowly day by day. There is no deterioration but progress is slow."
The health bulletin said Mother Teresa had thanked her team of doctors for their care.
"I am giving you so much trouble," the bulletin quoted her as saying. "I am so sorry. God bless you, all for Jesus, for the poorest of the poor."
